title: Geometry of the deformation
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), in the situation of
[def-pur-dnc-section-family] with $g:V\to B$ smooth of pure
relative dimension $d$ and $N_s\to B$ the normal bundle of the
section:

1. *the fibers.* The fiber of $\widetilde g$ over $1$ is
$(g:V\to B,s)$ and the fiber over $0$ is the
$\pi_N:N_s\to B$ with its zero section; hence by the
base-change compatibility of [def-pur-co-smoothness]
(applied to the closed immersions $i_1,i_0$ of the two
sections of $\mathbf A^1_B$),
$$
\qquad i_1^*F\simeq C(g,s),\qquad
i_0^*F\simeq C(\pi_N,0_N).\qquad\text{(the two fibers)}
$$
1. *the coordinates.* Since $s$ is a section of a smooth
map, etale-locally there are coordinates $x_1,\dots,x_d$ on
$V$ over $B$ in which $s$ is given by $x_i=0$ (the
relative form of the local linearization of
[lem-pur-regular-immersion-linearization], via
[sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form]); on the DNC chart the
coordinates are $u_i=x_i/t$, so $\widetilde g$ is smooth of
pure relative dimension $d$.
1. *the punctured trivialization.* Over $\mathbf G_{m,B}$
the deformation space is canonically
$$
D_sV|_{\mathbf G_{m,B}}\simeq V\times_B\mathbf G_{m,B},
\qquad \widetilde s|_{\mathbf G_{m,B}}=s\times 1,
$$
so base change for the cohomologically smooth $\widetilde g$
gives the canonical isomorphism
$$
\kappa^\circ:j^*F\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;j^*a^*C(g,s),
\qquad a:\mathbf A^1_B\to B.
$$
1. *the standard pair.* For the standard pair
$(\mathbf A^d_B\to B,0)$, the deformation space is
$\mathbf A^d_{B}\times_B\mathbf A^1_B$ with $x_k=tu_k$, the
family object is the pullback $a^*\bigl(0^*\omega_{\mathbf A^d_B/B}\bigr)$, and $0^*\omega_{\mathbf A^d_B/B}=\Lambda(d)[2d]$ by the vector-bundle purity of
[cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity].
1. *base change.* The Rees-algebra description of the
deformation space for a closed section, the punctured
trivialization, and the family object commute with base change
in $B$.

proof.text: For the finite purity coefficients of [def-pur-conventions], use the maximal-ideal membership and uniformizer-generation clauses of [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. The spectral absolute value of ell is its p-adic norm, strictly less than one. Hence ell lies in the maximal ideal, so ell^n lies in its nth power and vanishes in O_E/(varpi^n), including its ULift. Mathlib charP_of_card_eq_prime_pow gives characteristic p for k_0 from its recorded cardinality, and injectivity of k_0 to k gives characteristic p for k. Since ell and p are distinct primes, ell is nonzero in k and therefore a unit. Map this unit to global sections of T. This proves invertibleExponent without a ramification-index divisibility hypothesis.

For compactifiable, finite type of B over the field implies that B is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact (Mathlib LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian and QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace), hence quasi-separated. Apply [thm-nagata-compactification] to g. No new hypothesis or compactification datum is added.

For the normal projection use the canonical closed-immersion factorization purityNormalProjection of [def-pur-normal-bundle]. Its composite with s is the affine relative-gluing projection to V. Since s is separated, IsAffineHom.of_comp makes this projection to B affine. It equals the published normalConeProj g s by purityNormalProjection_eq and s followed by g equal to the identity. This gives normalQuasiCompact. The published normalConeData, obtained by base change from smoothOfRelativeDimension_deformationSpaceProj along t=0, supplies smoothness of relative dimension d. Affineness supplies separatedness and quasi-compactness, and smoothness supplies local finite type. Apply compactifiable to prove normalCompactifiable.

Retain the actual section-invariant and finite comparison realization of [def-pur-finite-section-comparison]. For sectionBaseChange, apply the general smooth exceptional base-change compatibility theorem isIso_rightDerivedUpperShriekBaseChangeMap_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_general of [prop-asd-smooth-base-change], retaining the upstream-sync public compatibility import, to the actual compact-support adjunction mate. Evaluate at the coefficient unit, pass to dualizingComplexBaseChangeMap using its IsIso equivalence, and compose the two canonical inverse-image composition isomorphisms along hs. This gives the displayed isomorphism, rather than choosing an arbitrary endpoint isomorphism.

For fibreOne and fibreZero, retain the published extended-Rees deformation space and its actual one- and zero-fibre pullback squares. Supply their smoothness from smoothOfRelativeDimension_deformationSpaceProj, coefficient invertibility from invertibleExponent, and compactifiability from compactifiable and normalCompactifiable. Apply sectionBaseChange to each square and the published augmentation-section identities. The local-coordinate, punctured-trivialization, standard-pair and geometric base-change calculations remain the existing upstream constructions imported through Coordinates and BaseChange; this module only assembles the canonical fibre comparisons. No unit-level step is replaced.

proof_origin.place: G3 stage-3 proof: coefficient exponent, Nagata domain checks, affine normal projection and canonical actual-fibre base-change maps; original unit route retained.

lean.statement: def sectionBaseChange (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ] {X Y X' Y' : Scheme.{u}} (d : ℕ) (f : X ⟶ Y) [HasCompactification f] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] [HasInvertibleExponent Λ X] {b : Y' ⟶ Y} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'} {a : X' ⟶ X} [HasCompactification f'] [QuasiCompact f'] (sq : IsPullback a f' f b) (s : Y ⟶ X) (s' : Y' ⟶ X') (hs : s' ≫ a = b ≫ s) : (Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) b).leftDerivedFunctor.obj (Etale.sectionInvariant Λ f s) ≅ Etale.sectionInvariant Λ f' s'
lean.note: The old arbitrary NormalConeData interface was unusable. Reuse the current actual extended-Rees geometry and construct the canonical section base-change and fibre maps from the adjunction mate, with the finite-type domain derived.
